title: Grok Outage: xAI Blames Memphis Data Center [2026]
summary: Grok Outage: xAI Blames Memphis Data Center [2026] Major AI Outage: Grok Trouble Tied to Memphis Data Center - Nadia Dubois - September 4, 2026 - AI & Machine Learning Nadia Dubois September 4, 2026 14 min read Grok, the chatbot built by Elon Musk’s xAI, went dark for users across X and its m
content: Grok, the chatbot built by Elon Musk’s xAI, went dark for users across X and its mobile apps on the morning of September 3, 2026, and the company says the blame sits squarely on its own hardware. In a statement flagged by Engadget, the SpaceXAI account apologized “for the issues you may have experienced with Grok following an outage at our Memphis compute center this morning,” adding that “all systems have now been restored and are functioning nominally.” PCMag, which first tied the disruption to the Memphis site in a report headlined “Grok Trouble Blamed on Outage at Memphis Data Center,” said the incident hit at the same time several other AI platforms were also struggling, a pattern also covered by MediaPost. Coverage of the outage also circulated through LADbible and Fox5 San Diego as the story spread beyond tech trade press into general news feeds. ... problems on September ... blamed on ... at its Memphis Compute ... Engadget ... or badly degraded, ... total platform blackout ... xAI’s Memphis campus, known as Colossus, has become one of the most closely watched data center projects in AI. PCMag reported that xAI powered up 100,000 Nvidia GPUs at the Memphis site specifically to train Grok, and the company has continued expanding the campus since, adding a second phase widely referred to as Colossus 2 alongside additional buildings in the surrounding area. The scale of the buildout is a big part of why any hiccup there ripples so widely: a facility built to run hundreds of thousands of GPUs concentrates an enormous amount of both compute and risk in one place. ... The September 3 event is not an isolated incident. PCMag documented a separate outage in mid-January 2026 in which Grok responded to queries with “No response” messages during broader issues affecting X. Infrastructure incident tracking referenced in industry reporting also pointed to a significant disruption around April 23, 2026, when Grok users saw “High Demand” errors and near-total unavailability for roughly four hours, an event that reporting linked to strain from integrating a Colossus cluster expansion at the same time xAI was training an upcoming Grok model. That same reporting characterized the April disruption as the fourth major service event for the Grok platform in 2026, following earlier issues in January, February and March. ... - Additional Memphis-linked disruptions are plausible as xAI continues expanding Colossus 2 and trains newer Grok model generations, following the same pattern seen around the April 2026 “High Demand” incident.
